how: The starter proposes a site, while recruitment and others' acceptance remain distinct acts rather than requirements of the role.
Open calls, named summons and renewed requests gather hands for initial and restarted flag attempts.
Participants choose a Breton mark, propose a better version and discuss the heart's position.
Participants report current progress, distinguish it from the target and locate a white-band start.
Coordinates, replacement image links and landmarks make proposed and ongoing work findable.
A renewed call receives a bare availability offer, while a design proposal receives bare assent.
Participants explicitly judge themselves too few to sustain duplicate projects.
A starter attributes removed fleurs de lys to an existing drawing's makers without independently identifying them.
A respondent dismisses occupied work as ugly and expendable, and the starter reports placing fleurs de lys there.
The second attempt is explicitly explained by the first flag being eaten, with a new location supplied.
Participants report complete loss and later link an image while describing a small vandalised but recognisable result.
A participant reports guest reliance on an authorised list and a prohibition protecting the host background without verifying enforcement.
A participant offers possible later help while explaining that their own war limits availability.
Protection promises and final damage do not establish enacted repair, its success or keepers undoing an agreed change through missing information.
Moving after resistance does not establish an explicit norm of sparing neighbours or an apology.
Reported authorisation on a host background does not expose border negotiations or an agreed truce.
Announcements and redirections identify attempts without establishing completion, celebration or collective credit.
The closing assessment records the result without specifying an effort or tie to carry forward.
The scripts warning concerns a threat to the distant flag rather than documented automation by its builders.
A conditional invitation and claimed Spanish support do not establish coalition membership or reciprocal defence.
Mentioning a war of their own does not identify a rival or show a sustained contest in talk.
Recruitment and internal chat invitations do not show moderation of canvas posts or objections to a flood.
The project misunderstanding does not show a dispute or stated limit concerning who can commit placers to inter-room terms.
The closing image and damage assessment neither contest cleanup nor correct a competing account of the work.
The playful claim about Breton absence does not establish a host takeover or recruitment framed as fake.
A friendly description of the Irish flag and resistance at occupied work do not establish an inherited quarrel.
Seeking flag representation does not establish beyond-the-flag politics, lore or colour faith.
Visible sequencing proposals and invitations to unseen planning cannot determine whether decided governance existed or was unnecessary.
The local clash does not identify a pre-canvas tie as the reason for overwriting.
Relaying a thread to an internal chat does not identify an envoy carrying a proposal to another room.
Internal invitations, planned thread relay and cross-venue identity confirmation now fit the chat candidate without implying a coalition or revealing chat decisions.
A participant identifies the design behind a faulty image link and seeks confirmation before another member supplies a replacement.
A respondent playfully exaggerates the flag's absence as an error to correct, without establishing a running gag or its invention here.
Before the first reported loss, participants propose a site using existing black and white and supply coordinates.
A participant fits involvement around going out by promising to return in the evening if the project starts.
An invitation to chat does not identify a newcomer whose viewing of the canvas mark brought them into the room.
Inviting people to the room's chat does not establish a new canvas-born faction forming around the mark.
Calling an occupied drawing ugly does not show dispute over slurs, offensive jokes or hate symbols.
Wanting a flag in the final image does not show outreach to creators, teams or the press.
Dismissing existing work as expendable does not establish an exchange arguing whether covering it is fair.
Going out and offering to return does not establish stressful withdrawal or a personal quarrel needing repair.
Open chat invitations do not establish hiding plans, infiltration or strategic language switching.
Attempt redirection and recruitment do not show objections to canvas posts prompting attacks on the room's own mark.
A nonworking external image link does not establish canvas-site faults or fixes to its controls.
Identity confirmation across chat and Reddit does not establish belonging to two rooms in a contest or at a border.
The starter supplies a proposed site and asks for help in the same turn, which another member answers.
A renewed request receives an explicit one-line offer to be available if needed.
A recruitment answer supplies coordinates on occupied work and dismisses that work as expendable.
A call and later progress reports do not identify building as an effect of that call.
A placed design receives a protection promise, but enacted upkeep following construction is not established.
A reported host rule does not reveal defence prompting border negotiations.
Reported host authorisation supplies neither observed border negotiation nor ensuing restraint by the guest.
A warning about threatening scripts cannot establish that upkeep led builders to automate their own placements.
Attempt announcements and progress reports do not establish a finished mark prompting completion observances.
Loss and outcome recording are visible without an evidenced completion ritual causing the recording.
The outcome record is not followed by a coded decision about what to carry forward.
Scarcity explains proposed project reunion, whereas loss explains the new attempt, leaving scarcity-driven relocation unestablished.
Design discussion and reference images do not establish a posted agreed pixel template settling the discussion.
A constrained offer to help someone else does not establish defence causing an appeal that delivered outside help.
The host-rule report and conditional aid offer do not expose border talk opening a completed exchange.
An initial willingness to overwrite is followed by relocation without an explicit refusal, apology or restraint appeal.
The response to resistance proposes moving rather than reporting a truce or negotiated alternative.
The reported clash does not expose a named rival or an ensuing contest of taunts and claims.
An offer constrained by the group's own war and claimed Spanish support do not establish defence causing coalition membership.
Repeated calls and chat invitations do not show a canvas flood causing posting restrictions.
The misunderstanding shows neither an inter-room agreement followed by refusal nor a disclaimer made while negotiating terms.
Reconcile duplicate unfinished builds by discovering the misunderstanding and inviting reunion before committing scarce hands.
Concentrating unfinished work depends on comparing duplicate projects and progress rather than simply choosing upkeep over expansion.
After explaining the new attempt through the first flag's loss, the starter renews the call for help.
A loss-explained fresh attempt returns to building through a current-state report and target image.
Announcements and cross-thread redirections keep unfinished attempts findable without establishing a completion ritual.
Allow an invitation and conditional future offer before an aid exchange whose recipient, acceptance and delivery remain unresolved.
